page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-2 is a compute-oriented virtual machine built on the 64-bit Arm architecture. The instance runs on ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 3.0 GHz, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. Hardware cache provisions include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an 80 MB L3 cache. System memory is sized at 4.0 GB, yielding a compute-optimized allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators, relying on network-attached storage solutions for disk operations.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-threaded performance alongside expected constraints from its two-core footprint. Single-core data processing tests show strong throughput, delivering 32.27 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 13.96 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Single-core stress-ng tests place the instance in the middle 50% category with a score of 1818.68. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded metrics scale proportionally to its core count, with multi-core stress-ng scoring 3616.42 and multi-threaded bzip3 reaching 27.33 GB/sec, placing it in lower benchmark quartiles. Memory bandwidth achieves 56.53 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads, while large-block write operations average 21.88 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure and resource efficiency perspective, the c4a-highcpu-2 provides dedicated Arm core execution without the multi-tenant performance variance associated with shared-core instances. The compact 4.0 GB memory envelope and lack of local NVMe storage restrict suitability for large in-memory caching tiers or database-heavy workloads, as reflected by moderate database operations results and Redis throughput measuring 4.4 million operations per second. The server profile aligns with lightweight stateless workloads, dedicated microservices, API proxies, static web serving pipelines, and isolated continuous integration testing tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-2 is a compute-focused instance featuring 2 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the instance provides 4.0 GB of RAM alongside 80 MB of L3 cache. It lacks onboard local storage and hardware GPU acceleration, requiring networked block storage for persistence. Benchmark results indicate competitive single-threaded capabilities, evidenced by strong gzip compression and bzip3 decompression throughput. However, overall multi-core compute throughput and memory write bandwidth reflect the limits of its dual-core topology, landing in lower percentile tiers on multi-threaded stress testing and Redis operations. Because of its lean memory profile and absence of local disks, the c4a-highcpu-2 offers a cost-effective hardware footprint best suited for lightweight web serving, stateless microservices, background task workers, and small-scale compilation pipelines.
